page: Vultr vx1-g-96c-384g is an x86_64 cloud server instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 96 dedicated AMD vCPUs paired with 384.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB allocated per vCPU. The server configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not contain discrete GPU hardware.

The instance is equipped with a minimal 1 GB NVMe SSD local storage footprint. Because this local volume is negligible in capacity, practical deployment models necessitate reliance on network-attached storage or stateless architectures. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the resource profile concentrates value entirely into high core density and dedicated CPU throughput rather than bundled disk capacity.

Due to the balanced vCPU-to-memory relationship and the lack of sizable local storage, this server is suitable for horizontally scaled web services, parallel compilation pipelines, distributed analytics engines, and in-memory computing workloads that access independent network storage.
